steps.reasoning_content:
The user wants me to restore the RTL implementation files in `src/` for the PULP common_cells library. This is a massive task - ~80 SystemVerilog files have been emptied and need to be reimplemented.

Key points:
1. Partial credit is available - I don't need to complete everything
2. Tests are: Verilator lint for each module (~65) + 2 ECC functional tests
3. I should start with simpler modules and work outward
4. I have up to 24 hours

My strategy should be:
1. First, check what files exist and what the test structure looks like
2. Read README.md to understand module descriptions
3. Read a few simple testbenches to understand interfaces
4. Implement simple modules first (popcount, lzc, binary_to_gray, gray_to_binary, etc.)
5. Gradually work up to more complex modules

Let me start by exploring the directory structure and understanding what's available.

133: ## Header Contents
134: 
135: This repository currently contains the following header files.
136: 
137: ### RTL Register Macros
138: 
139: The header file [`registers.svh`](include/common_cells/registers.svh) contains macros that expand to descriptions of registers.
140: To avoid misuse of `always_ff` blocks, only the following macros shall be used to describe sequential behavior.
141: The use of linter rules that flag explicit uses of `always_ff` in source code is encouraged.
142: 
143: |    Macro     |                             Arguments                             |                                Description                                |
144: | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
145: | <code>`FF</code>     | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, (`clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`)             | Flip-flop with asynchronous active-low reset                              |
146: | <code>`FFAR</code>   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arst_sig`                | Flip-flop with asynchronous active-high reset                             |
147: | <code>`FFARN</code>  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`               | *deprecated* Flip-flop with asynchronous active-low reset                 |
148: | <code>`FFSR</code>   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rst_sig`                 | Flip-flop with synchronous active-high reset                              |
149: | <code>`FFSRN</code>  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rstn_sig`                | Flip-flop with synchronous active-low reset                               |
150: | <code>`FFNR</code>   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `clk_sig`                                       | Flip-flop without reset                                                   |
151: |              |                                                                   |                                                                           |
152: | <code>`FFL</code>    | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, (`clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`) | Flip-flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset              |
153: | <code>`FFLAR</code>  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arst_sig`    | Flip-flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-high reset             |
154: | <code>`FFLARN</code> | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`   | *deprecated* Flip-flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset |
155: | <code>`FFLSR</code>  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rst_sig`     | Flip-flop with load-enable and synchronous active-high reset              |
156: | <code>`FFLSRN</code> | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rstn_sig`    | Flip-flop with load-enable and synchronous active-low reset               |
157: | <code>`FFLNR</code>  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `clk_sig`                           | Flip-flop with load-enable without reset                                  |
158: - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*
159: - *Argument suffix `_sig` indicates signal names for present and next state as well as clocks and resets.*
160: - *Argument `rst_val` specifies the value literal to be assigned upon reset.*
161: - *Argument `load_ena` specifies the boolean expression that forms the load enable of the register.*

163: ### SystemVerilog Assertion Macros
164: 
165: The header file [`assertions.svh`](include/common_cells/assertions.svh) contains macros that expand to assertion blocks.
166: These macros should recduce the effort in writing many assertions and make it
167: easier to use them. They are similar to but incompatible with the macros used by [lowrisc](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_assert.sv).
168: 
169: #### Simple Assertion and Cover Macros
170: | Macro              | Arguments                                        | Description                                                                |
171: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

109: // Always-enable Flip-Flop without reset
110: // __q: Q output of FF
111: // __d: D input of FF
112: // __clk: clock input
113: `define FFNR(__q, __d, __clk)        \
114:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk)) begin \
115:     __q <= (__d);                    \
116:   end
117: 
118: // Flip-Flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset (implicit clock and reset)
119: // __q: Q output of FF
120: // __d: D input of FF
121: // __load: load d value into FF
122: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
123: // (__clk: clock input)
124: // (__arst_n: asynchronous reset, active-low)
125: `define FFL(__q, __d, __load, __reset_value, __clk = `REG_DFLT_CLK, __arst_n = `REG_DFLT_RST) \
126:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk) or negedge (__arst_n)) begin                                    \
127:     if (!__arst_n) begin                                                                      \
128:       __q <= (__reset_value);                                                                 \
129:     end else begin                                                                            \
130:       if (__load) begin                                                                       \
131:         __q <= (__d);                                                                         \
132:       end                                                                                     \
133:     end                                                                                       \
134:   end
135: 
136: // Flip-Flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-high reset
137: // __q: Q output of FF
138: // __d: D input of FF
139: // __load: load d value into FF
140: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
141: // __clk: clock input
142: // __arst: asynchronous reset, active-high
143: `define FFLAR(__q, __d, __load, __reset_value, __clk, __arst) \
144:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk) or posedge (__arst)) begin      \
145:     if (__arst) begin                                         \
146:       __q <= (__reset_value);                                 \
147:     end else begin                                            \
148:       if (__load) begin                                       \
149:         __q <= (__d);                                         \
150:       end                                                     \
151:     end                                                       \
152:   end
153: 
154: // DEPRECATED - use `FFL instead
155: // Flip-Flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset
156: // __q: Q output of FF
157: // __d: D input of FF
158: // __load: load d value into FF
159: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
160: // __clk: clock input
161: // __arst_n: asynchronous reset, active-low
162: `define FFLARN(__q, __d, __load, __reset_value, __clk, __arst_n) \
163:   `FFL(__q, __d, __load, __reset_value, __clk, __arst_n)
164: 
165: // Flip-Flop with load-enable and synchronous active-high reset
166: // __q: Q output of FF
167: // __d: D input of FF
168: // __load: load d value into FF
169: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
170: // __clk: clock input
171: // __reset_clk: reset input, active-high
172: `define FFLSR(__q, __d, __load, __reset_value, __clk, __reset_clk) \
173:   `ifndef NO_SYNOPSYS_FF                                           \
174:   /``* synopsys sync_set_reset `"__reset_clk`" *``/                \
175:   `endif                                                           \
176:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk)) begin                               \
177:     if (__reset_clk) begin                                         \
178:       __q <= (__reset_value);                                      \
179:     end else if (__load) begin                                     \
180:       __q <= (__d);                                                \
181:     end                                                            \
182:   end
183: 
184: // Flip-Flop with load-enable and synchronous active-low reset
185: // __q: Q output of FF
186: // __d: D input of FF
187: // __load: load d value into FF
188: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
189: // __clk: clock input
190: // __reset_n_clk: reset input, active-low
191: `define FFLSRN(__q, __d, __load, __reset_value, __clk, __reset_n_clk) \
192:   `ifndef NO_SYNOPSYS_FF                                              \
193:   /``* synopsys sync_set_reset `"__reset_n_clk`" *``/                 \
194:   `endif                                                              \
195:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk)) begin                                  \
196:     if (!__reset_n_clk) begin                                         \
197:       __q <= (__reset_value);                                         \
198:     end else if (__load) begin                                        \
199:       __q <= (__d);                                                   \
200:     end                                                               \
201:   end
202: 
203: // Flip-Flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset and synchronous clear
204: // __q: Q output of FF
205: // __d: D input of FF
206: // __load: load d value into FF
207: // __clear: assign reset value into FF
208: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
209: // __clk: clock input
210: // __arst_n: asynchronous reset, active-low
211: `define FFLARNC(__q, __d, __load, __clear, __reset_value, __clk, __arst_n) \
212:     `ifndef NO_SYNOPSYS_FF                                                 \
213:   /``* synopsys sync_set_reset `"__clear`" *``/                            \
214:     `endif                                                                 \
215:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk) or negedge (__arst_n)) begin                 \
216:     if (!__arst_n) begin                                                   \
217:       __q <= (__reset_value);                                              \
218:     end else begin                                                         \
219:       if (__clear) begin                                                   \
220:         __q <= (__reset_value);                                            \
221:       end else if (__load) begin                                           \
222:         __q <= (__d);                                                      \
223:       end                                                                  \
224:     end                                                                    \
225:   end
226: 
227: // Flip-Flop with asynchronous active-low reset and synchronous clear
228: // __q: Q output of FF
229: // __d: D input of FF
230: // __clear: assign reset value into FF
231: // __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
232: // __clk: clock input
233: // __arst_n: asynchronous reset, active-low
234: `define FFARNC(__q, __d, __clear, __reset_value, __clk, __arst_n) \
235:     `ifndef NO_SYNOPSYS_FF                                        \
236:   /``* synopsys sync_set_reset `"__clear`" *``/                   \
237:     `endif                                                        \
238:   always_ff @(posedge (__clk) or negedge (__arst_n)) begin        \
239:     if (!__arst_n) begin                                          \
240:       __q <= (__reset_value);                                     \
241:     end else begin                                                \
242:       if (__clear) begin                                          \
243:         __q <= (__reset_value);                                   \
244:       end else begin                                              \
245:         __q <= (__d);                                             \
246:       end                                                         \
247:     end                                                           \
248:   end

253: // __load: load d value into FF

11: // Testbench for generic FIFO
12: module fifo_inst_tb #(
13:     // FIFO parameters
14:     parameter bit           FALL_THROUGH,
15:     parameter int unsigned  DEPTH,
16:     parameter int unsigned  DATA_WIDTH = 8,
17:     // TB parameters
18:     parameter int unsigned  N_CHECKS,
19:     parameter time          TA,
20:     parameter time          TT
21: ) (
22:     input  logic    clk_i,
23:     input  logic    rst_ni,
24:     output logic    done_o
25: );
26: 
27:     import rand_verif_pkg::rand_wait;
28: 
29:     typedef logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] data_t;
30: 
31:     logic           clk,
32:                     flush,
33:                     full,
34:                     empty,
35:                     push,
36:                     pop,
37:                     try_push,
38:                     try_pop;
39: 
40:     data_t          wdata,
41:                     rdata;
42: 
43:     int unsigned    n_checks = 0;
44: 
45:     assign clk = clk_i;
46: 
47:     fifo_v3 #(
48:         .FALL_THROUGH   ( FALL_THROUGH  ),
49:         .DATA_WIDTH     ( DATA_WIDTH    ),
50:         .DEPTH          ( DEPTH         )
51:     ) dut (
52:         .clk_i,
53:         .rst_ni,
54:         .flush_i        ( flush         ),
55:         .testmode_i     ( 1'b0          ),
56:         .full_o         ( full          ),
57:         .empty_o        ( empty         ),
58:         .usage_o        (               ),
59:         .data_i         ( wdata         ),
60:         .push_i         ( push          ),
61:         .data_o         ( rdata         ),
62:         .pop_i          ( pop           )
63:     );
64: 
65:     // Simulation information and stopping.
66:     // TODO: Better stop after certain coverage is reached.
67:     initial begin
68:         done_o = 1'b0;
69:         $display("%m: Running test with FALL_THROUGH=%0d, DEPTH=%0d", FALL_THROUGH, DEPTH);
70:         wait (n_checks >= N_CHECKS);
71:         done_o = 1'b1;
72:         $display("%m: Checked %0d stimuli", n_checks);
73:     end
74: 
75:     class random_action_t;
76:         rand logic [1:0] action;
77:         constraint random_action {
78:             action dist {
79:                 0 := 40,
80:                 1 := 40,
81:                 3 := 2,
82:                 0 := 0
83:             };
84:         }
85:     endclass
86: 
87:     // Input driver: push, wdata, and flush
88:     assign push = try_push & ~full;
89:     initial begin
90:         automatic random_action_t rand_act = new();
91:         flush       <= 1'b0;
92:         wdata       <= 'x;
93:         try_push    <= 1'b0;
94:         wait (rst_ni);
95:         forever begin
96:             static logic rand_success;
97:             rand_wait(1, 8, clk);
98:             rand_success = rand_act.randomize(); assert(rand_success);
99:             case (rand_act.action)
100:                 0: begin // new random data and try to push
101:                     wdata       <= #TA $random();
102:                     try_push    <= #TA 1'b1;
103:                 end
104:                 1: begin // new random data but do not try to push
105:                     wdata       <= #TA $random();
106:                     try_push    <= #TA 1'b0;
107:                 end
108:                 2: begin // flush
109:                     flush       <= #TA 1'b1;
110:                     rand_wait(1, 8, clk);
111:                     flush       <= #TA 1'b0;
112:                 end
113:             endcase
114:         end
115:     end
116: 
117:     // Output driver: pop
118:     assign pop = try_pop & ~empty;
119:     initial begin
120:         try_pop <= 1'b0;
121:         wait (rst_ni);
122:         forever begin
123:             rand_wait(1, 8, clk);
124:             try_pop <= #TA $random();
125:         end
126:     end
127: 
128:     // Monitor & checker: model expected response and check against actual response
129:     initial begin
130:         data_t queue[$];
131:         wait (rst_ni);
132:         forever begin
133:             @(posedge clk_i);
134:             #(TT);
135:             if (flush) begin
136:                 queue = {};
137:             end else begin
138:                 if (push && !full) begin
139:                     queue.push_back(wdata);
140:                 end
141:                 if (pop && !empty) begin
142:                     automatic data_t data = queue.pop_front();
143:                     assert (rdata == data) else $error("Queue output %0x != %0x", rdata, data);
144:                     n_checks++;
145:                 end
146:             end
147:         end
148:     end
149: 
150: // https://github.com/verilator/verilator/issues/5981
151: `ifndef VERILATOR
152:     if (FALL_THROUGH) begin
153:         // In fall through mode, assert that the output data is equal to the input data when pushing
154:         // to an empty FIFO.
155:         assert property (@(posedge clk_i) ((empty & ~push) ##1 push) |-> rdata == wdata)
156:             else $error("Input did not fall through");
157:     end
158: `endif
159: 
160: endmodule
161: 
162: // Testbench for different FIFO configurations
163: module fifo_tb #(
164:     // TB parameters
165:     parameter int unsigned  N_CHECKS        = 100000,
166:     parameter time          TCLK            = 10ns,
167:     parameter time          TA              = TCLK * 1/4,
168:     parameter time          TT              = TCLK * 3/4
169: );
170: 
171:     logic       clk,
172:                 rst_n;

13: // Test bench for the counting bloom filter
14: // Randomly puts in data items into the filter.
15: // Removes the put in items after some time.
16: // One random lookup in each cycle.
17: // The testbench has a `control_array`, which serves as the golden model for the lookups.
18: // Each time a value gets put or removed into the filter, the array gets updated.
19: // On each lookup in the DUT it gets cross checked with the array.
20: // The test bench keeps book for each lookup and prints at the end the number of lookups,
21: // and the number of positive, false positive, negative and false negative lookups.
22: // The number of false negatives has to be 0 as it would indicate that the lookup was negative,
23: // even when the data was put in the filter. False positives are ok, because they are the result
24: // of hash-collisions, inherent to a counting bloom filter.
25: 
26: module cb_filter_tb;
27:   // TB parameters
28:   localparam time TCycle = 10ns;
29:   localparam time TAppli =  2ns;
30:   localparam time TTest  =  8ns;
31:   localparam int unsigned RunCycles  = 10000000;
32: 
33:   // DUT parameters
34:   localparam int unsigned NoHashes    = 32'd3;
35:   localparam int unsigned HashWidth   = 32'd6;
36:   localparam int unsigned HashRounds  = 32'd1;
37:   localparam int unsigned DataWidth   = 32'd11;
38:   localparam int unsigned BucketWidth = 32'd3;
39: 
40:   typedef logic [DataWidth-1:0] data_t;
41: 
42:   localparam cb_filter_pkg::cb_seed_t [NoHashes-1:0] Seeds = '{
43:     '{PermuteSeed: 32'd299034753, XorSeed: 32'd4094834 },
44:     '{PermuteSeed: 32'd19921030,  XorSeed: 32'd995713  },
45:     '{PermuteSeed: 32'd294388,    XorSeed: 32'd65146511}
46:   };
47: 
48: //---------------------------------------------------------
49: // Associative array as model
50: //---------------------------------------------------------
51:   logic control_array [*];
52:   int unsigned max_items;
53:   int unsigned min_items;
54: 
55: //---------------------------------------------------------
56: // Bookkeeping
57: //---------------------------------------------------------
58:   longint unsigned no_tests;
59:   longint unsigned no_positives;
60:   longint unsigned no_false_positives;
61:   longint unsigned no_negatives;
62:   longint unsigned no_false_negatives;
63: 
64: //---------------------------------------------------------
65: // DUT signals
66: //---------------------------------------------------------
67:   logic  clk;
68:   logic  rst_n;
69:   logic  sim_done;
70: 
71:   data_t look_data;
72:   logic  look_valid;
73:   data_t incr_data;
74:   logic  incr_valid;
75:   data_t decr_data;
76:   logic  decr_valid;
77: 
78:   logic                  filter_clear;
79:   logic  [HashWidth-1:0] filter_usage;
80:   logic                  filter_full,  filter_empty, filter_error;
81: 
82:   // -------------
83:   // Clock generator
84:   // -------------
85:   clk_rst_gen #(
86:     .ClkPeriod     ( TCycle ),
87:     .RstClkCycles  (      5 )
88:   ) i_clk_gen (
89:     .clk_o  (   clk ),
90:     .rst_no ( rst_n )
91:   );
92: 
93:   // ------------------------
94:   // Test Bench
95:   // ------------------------
96:   initial begin : stimulus
97:     sim_done = 1'b0;
98:     no_tests           = 64'd0;
99:     no_positives       = 64'd0;
100:     no_false_positives = 64'd0;
101:     no_negatives       = 64'd0;
102:     no_false_negatives = 64'd0;
103:     init_signals();
104:     fork
105:       begin
106:         // simulation control branch
107:         max_items = 10;
108:         min_items =  3;
109:         @(posedge rst_n);
110:         repeat (RunCycles) @(posedge clk);
111:         sim_done = 1'b1;
112:       end
113:       begin
114:         @(posedge rst_n);
115:         run_lookup(sim_done);
116:       end
117:       begin
118:         @(posedge rst_n);
119:         run_increment(sim_done, decr_valid);
120:       end
121:       begin
122:         @(posedge rst_n);
123:         run_decrement(sim_done);
124:       end
125:     join
126:     print_result(no_tests, no_positives, no_false_positives, no_negatives, no_false_negatives);
127:     empty_filter();
128:     $stop();
129:   end
130: 
131:   task cycle_start();
132:     #TTest;
133:   endtask : cycle_start
134: 
135:   task cycle_end();
136:     @(posedge clk);
137:   endtask : cycle_end
138: 
139:   task reset_filter();
140:     filter_clear <= #TAppli '1;
141:     cycle_end();
142:     filter_clear <= #TAppli '0;
143:   endtask : reset_filter
144: 
145:   task init_signals();
146:     look_data    <= #TAppli '0;
147:     incr_data    <= #TAppli '0;
148:     incr_valid   <= #TAppli '0;
149:     decr_data    <= #TAppli '0;
150:     decr_valid   <= #TAppli '0;
151:     filter_clear <= #TAppli '0;
152:   endtask : init_signals
153: 
154:   // runs each cycle a lookup and tests if the output is expected
155:   task automatic run_lookup(ref logic sim_done);
156:     while (!sim_done) begin
157:       logic [DataWidth-1:0] lookup = $urandom_range(0,2**DataWidth-1);;
158:       rand_wait(0,6);
159:       look_data    <= #TAppli lookup;
160:       cycle_start();
161:       no_tests++;
162:       // check the result
163:       if(control_array.exists(lookup)) begin
164:         // the result has to be right
165:         if(!look_valid) begin
166:           $warning(1, "Had a false negative!!!\nIndex: %d", lookup);
167:           no_false_negatives++;
168:         end else begin
169:           no_positives++;
170:         end
171:       end else begin
172:         // here we can check for false positives
173:         if(look_valid) begin
174:           //$display("Had a false positive!\nIndex: %d", lookup);
175:           no_false_positives++;
176:         end else begin
177:           //$display("Item correctly not in Set.\nIndex: %d", lookup);
178:           no_negatives++;
179:         end
180:       end
181:       cycle_end();
182:     end
183:   endtask : run_lookup
184: 
185:   // randomly put data into the filter
186:   task automatic run_increment(ref logic sim_done, ref logic decr_valid);
187:     while (!sim_done) begin
188:       logic [DataWidth-1:0] data = $urandom_range(0,2**DataWidth-1);
189:       if(!control_array.exists(data)) begin
190:         rand_wait(0,5);
191:         incr_data <= #TAppli data;
192:         while (filter_full | (control_array.num() > max_items))
193:             begin if (sim_done | decr_valid) break; cycle_end(); end
194:         incr_valid <= #TAppli 1'b1;
195:         cycle_end();
196:         control_array[data] = 1'b1;
197:         incr_data  <= #TAppli '0;
198:         incr_valid <= #TAppli '0;
199:       end else begin
200:         cycle_end();
201:       end
202:     end
203:   endtask : run_increment
204: 
205:   // remove randomly an item from the filter
206:   task automatic run_decrement(ref logic sim_done);
207:     int unsigned nb_tryes = 0;
208:     while (!sim_done) begin
209:       logic [DataWidth-1:0] data = $urandom_range(0,2**DataWidth-1);;
210:       if(control_array.exists(data)) begin
211:         if(control_array.num() > min_items) begin
212:           rand_wait(0,5);
213:           decr_data  <= #TAppli data;
214:           decr_valid <= #TAppli 1'b1;
215:           cycle_start();
216:           control_array.delete(data);
217:           cycle_end();
218:           decr_data  <= #TAppli '0;
219:           decr_valid <= #TAppli 1'b0;
220:         end else begin
221:           cycle_end();
222:         end
223:       end else begin
224:         if(nb_tryes < 100) begin
225:           nb_tryes++;
226:         end else begin
227:           nb_tryes = 0;
228:           cycle_end();
229:         end
230:       end
231:     end
232:   endtask : run_decrement
233: 
234:   // clear the filter from all items
235:   task empty_filter();
236:     rand_wait(10,15);
237:     for (int unsigned i = 0; i < 2**DataWidth; i++) begin
238:       if(control_array.exists(i)) begin
239:         decr_data  <= #TAppli i;
240:         decr_valid <= #TAppli 1'b1;
241:         cycle_start();
242:         control_array.delete(i);
243:         cycle_end();
244:       end
245:     end
246:     // check empty flag
247:     decr_data  <= #TAppli '0;
248:     decr_valid <= #TAppli 1'b0;
249:     cycle_start();
250:     cycle_end();
251:     $display("Filter empty is: %b", filter_empty);
252:   endtask : empty_filter
253: 
254:   task print_result(input longint unsigned n_test, n_pos, n_f_pos, n_neg, n_f_neg);
255:     $info(   "######################################################");
256:     if (n_f_neg == 64'h0) begin
257:       $display("***SUCCESS***");
258:     end else begin
259:       $display("!!!FAILED!!!");
260:     end
261:     $display("Finished Tests");
262:     $display("NO Testes:    %d", n_test);
263:     $display("NO Positive:  %d", n_pos);
264:     $display("NO False Pos: %d", n_f_pos);
265:     $display("NO Negatives: %d", n_neg);
266:     $display("NO False Neg: %d <--- Success if this is 0!", n_f_neg);
267:     $display("######################################################");
268:   endtask : print_result
269: 
270:   task automatic rand_wait(input int unsigned min, max);
271:     int unsigned rand_success, cycles;
272:     rand_success = std::randomize(cycles) with {
273:       cycles >= min;
274:       cycles <= max;
275:     };
276:     assert (rand_success) else $error("Failed to randomize wait cycles!");
277:     repeat (cycles) @(posedge clk);
278:   endtask : rand_wait
279: 
280: 
281:   cb_filter #(
282:     .KHashes       ( NoHashes    ), // Number of hash functions
283:     .HashWidth     ( HashWidth   ), // Number of counters is 2**HASH_WIDTH
284:     .HashRounds    ( HashRounds  ),
285:     .InpWidth      ( DataWidth   ), // Input data width
286:     .BucketWidth   ( BucketWidth ), // Width of Bucket counters
287:     .Seeds         ( Seeds       )
288:   ) i_dut (
289:     .clk_i  ( clk   ),  // Clock
290:     .rst_ni ( rst_n ),  // Active low reset
291:     // data lookup
292:     .look_data_i    ( look_data    ),
293:     .look_valid_o   ( look_valid   ),
294:     // data increment
295:     .incr_data_i    ( incr_data    ),
296:     .incr_valid_i   ( incr_valid   ),
297:     // data decrement
298:     .decr_data_i    ( decr_data    ),
299:     .decr_valid_i   ( decr_valid   ),
300:     // status signals
301:     .filter_clear_i ( filter_clear ),
302:     .filter_usage_o ( filter_usage ),
303:     .filter_full_o  ( filter_full  ),
304:     .filter_empty_o ( filter_empty ),
305:     .filter_error_o ( filter_error )
306:   );
307: endmodule
